title: China-to-South Korea Air-source Heat Pump Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: KEMCO Mandatory Energy Efficiency Grade — Grade 1 to Grade 5
rows.target_requirement: South Korea requires covered heat-pump and air-conditioning products to comply with the KEMCO energy efficiency labelling framework before market placement. The label uses a Grade 1 to Grade 5 scale, with Grade 1 as the highest grade, and product classification, test data, model registration, and Korean label content must follow Korean rules rather than China label categories.
target_standards: KEMCO energy efficiency labelling and standards programme
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly relies on GB 25454 and GB/T 7725 for heat-pump and air-conditioner COP, SCOP, and performance evidence, CCC mandatory certification for applicable heat pumps up to 40 kW, and GB 9237 as a refrigerant safety baseline. China Energy Label values are not automatically mapped to South Korea's KEMCO Grade 1 to Grade 5 label.
china_standards: CCC mandatory certification for applicable heat pumps up to 40 kW
rows.gap: Chinese GB efficiency reports may be useful engineering inputs, but exporters still need Korean classification, Korean test conditions, KEMCO registration data, Korean energy-label artwork, and grade calculation. Grade 1 is the highest grade in South Korea, so claims must not reuse China grade terminology without recalculation.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for covered heat-pump and air-conditioning products under KEMCO energy efficiency labelling rules
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for applicable Chinese energy efficiency categories; not equivalent to KEMCO grade

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Major gap — KEMCO energy-efficiency grade labelling is a South Korea-specific market requirement; China efficiency data must be reclassified and recalculated.

source.publisher: Korea Energy Agency / KEMCO Energy Efficiency Programme

rows.requirement: Korean Performance Testing — SCOP, COP, Capacity, and 60 Hz Supply
rows.target_requirement: South Korea's energy-efficiency assessment for heat-pump HVAC products must reflect Korean product classes, rated capacities, seasonal performance metrics such as SCOP where applicable, and the Korean power system of 220 V single-phase residential supply or 380 V three-phase commercial supply at 60 Hz. China-market 50 Hz compressor, fan, inverter, and control designs require South Korea-specific validation.
target_standards: KEMCO energy efficiency test and registration rules
Korean 220 V / 380 V, 60 Hz supply conditions
Applicable KS C IEC heat-pump and air-conditioner standards
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly relies on GB 25454 and GB/T 7725 for COP, SCOP, capacity, and performance evidence, CCC mandatory certification for applicable heat pumps up to 40 kW, and GB 9237 as a refrigerant safety baseline. China domestic testing typically assumes China-market electrical design conditions and does not prove 60 Hz Korean compatibility.
china_standards: CCC mandatory certification for applicable heat pumps up to 40 kW
rows.gap: The voltage label may look similar for residential products because both China and South Korea use nominal 220 V, but the frequency difference is critical. A China 50 Hz heat pump cannot be treated as directly compatible with South Korea's 60 Hz grid without compressor, motor, inverter, protection, heating performance, noise, and durability validation.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where Korean energy-efficiency registration or product safety evidence depends on rated performance and electrical supply conditions
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for applicable Chinese efficiency and CCC evidence; does not prove Korean 60 Hz operation

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Critical gap — Korean energy and performance evidence must be generated or validated for 60 Hz operation; China 50 Hz heat-pump designs are not directly compatible.

rows.requirement: KC Mandatory Certification — ECPSA and KATS Scope
rows.target_requirement: South Korea requires in-scope electrical appliances and consumer products to obtain KC certification before sale under the Electrical Appliances and Consumer Products Safety Control Act, with KATS overseeing the safety framework. Heat-pump HVAC products must be assessed for KC Mark applicability, Korean model registration, Korean-language markings, factory and importer obligations, and adopted KS C IEC standards such as KS C IEC 60335-2-40 for heat-pump and air-conditioning safety.
target_standards: Electrical Appliances and Consumer Products Safety Control Act (ECPSA)
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly relies on GB 25454 and GB/T 7725 for heat-pump and air-conditioner efficiency and performance evidence, CCC mandatory certification for applicable heat pumps up to 40 kW, and GB 9237 as a refrigerant safety baseline. These Chinese documents support domestic compliance but are not recognized as KC certification evidence for South Korea.
china_standards: CCC mandatory certification for applicable heat pumps up to 40 kW
rows.gap: CCC is not recognized as KC. Chinese exporters must prepare a South Korea-specific KC certification package, confirm KS C IEC 60335-2-40 alignment, identify in-scope components, provide Korean markings and manuals, and support importer or local representative obligations. The finished product also needs 60 Hz compatibility evidence because China-market 50 Hz compressor designs are not directly compatible with South Korea.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for in-scope heat-pump HVAC products and covered electrical components under ECPSA / KC
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for applicable Chinese domestic-market heat pumps under CCC; not equivalent to KC

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Major gap — KC certification and Korean safety documentation are required where ECPSA applies; CCC certificates and GB reports do not replace KC.

source.publisher: Korea Product Safety Management Institute / Safety Korea

rows.requirement: Refrigerant Registration and HFC Controls — KEC / MOE Fluorine Management Act
rows.target_requirement: South Korea controls fluorinated refrigerants through KEC / MOE administration under the Fluorine Management Act and related HFC phase-down policy. Heat-pump products using fluorinated refrigerants may require Korean documentation for refrigerant type, charge amount, GWP, import or handling controls, labelling, recovery, and downstream service obligations.
target_standards: MOE fluorinated gas and HFC phase-down measures
Korean refrigerant registration and handling controls
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly relies on GB 25454 and GB/T 7725 for heat-pump and air-conditioner performance evidence, CCC mandatory certification for applicable heat pumps up to 40 kW, and GB 9237 as a refrigerant safety baseline. China refrigerant safety or product-label evidence does not replace South Korea refrigerant registration, handling, or HFC phase-down documentation.
china_standards: CCC mandatory certification for applicable heat pumps up to 40 kW
rows.gap: The South Korea gap is lifecycle documentation, not only refrigerant safety. Exporters should identify whether the refrigerant itself, pre-charged equipment, importer activity, installation, servicing, recovery, and disposal create Korean registration or reporting obligations.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where fluorinated refrigerant content, import, handling, recovery, or reporting falls within KEC / MOE controls
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory or policy-controlled depending on China refrigerant and product context; not equivalent to Korean refrigerant registration

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Gap — refrigerant documentation must be mapped to South Korea KEC / MOE controls; GB 9237 and China product labels are not enough by themselves.

source.publisher: Ministry of Environment, Republic of Korea

rows.requirement: Allowed and Phasing-out Refrigerants — R-32, R-410A, and R-22
rows.target_requirement: For South Korea market planning, R-32 and R-410A remain usable refrigerants for many heat-pump applications subject to applicable safety, registration, labelling, and HFC management controls, while R-22 is being phased out and should not be treated as a normal new-product refrigerant choice. Refrigerant selection also affects KC safety evaluation under KS C IEC 60335-2-40.
target_standards: KS C IEC 60335-2-40 refrigerant safety provisions
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly relies on GB 25454 and GB/T 7725 for performance evidence, CCC mandatory certification for applicable heat pumps up to 40 kW, and GB 9237 as a refrigerant safety baseline. A refrigerant allowed or historically used in China does not automatically satisfy South Korea's phase-down, labelling, or safety documentation expectations.
china_standards: CCC mandatory certification for applicable heat pumps up to 40 kW
rows.gap: Chinese exporters should avoid assuming that an R-22 legacy design can be exported as a normal Korean-market product. R-32 and R-410A designs still need Korean charge-limit, flammability, leakage, marking, service, and recovery review, particularly where the product is redesigned for 60 Hz compressors.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where refrigerant choice affects Korean safety, registration, phase-down, labelling, service, or recovery duties
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for applicable China refrigerant safety baseline and product evidence; not equivalent to Korean refrigerant controls

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Gap — R-32 and R-410A may be usable but still need Korean review, while R-22 phase-out makes legacy designs high risk for new South Korea exports.

rows.requirement: Electrical Safety, EMC, and Grid Compatibility — 220 V / 380 V at 60 Hz
rows.target_requirement: South Korea uses 220 V single-phase residential supply and 380 V three-phase commercial supply at 60 Hz. Heat-pump HVAC products must demonstrate electrical safety and grid compatibility for these Korean conditions, and EMC obligations may involve MSIT / KCC rules in addition to KC safety under KATS. KS C IEC standards are adopted for relevant safety testing.
target_standards: South Korea 220 V / 380 V, 60 Hz grid conditions
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly relies on GB 25454 and GB/T 7725 for efficiency and performance, CCC mandatory certification for applicable heat pumps up to 40 kW, and GB 9237 as a refrigerant safety baseline. China-market electrical evidence generally reflects 50 Hz product design and does not by itself prove South Korea 60 Hz safety, EMC, compressor, inverter, or control compatibility.
china_standards: CCC mandatory certification for applicable heat pumps up to 40 kW
rows.gap: This is a critical design gap. Residential nominal voltage is similar to China at 220 V, but South Korea is 60 Hz, so China 50 Hz heat pumps should be treated as incompatible until the compressor, motors, inverter drive, protection devices, thermal performance, EMC, noise, and marking package are validated for Korea.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for Korean KC safety, EMC, installation, and energy-performance evidence where electrical supply conditions affect compliance
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for applicable CCC and China GB evidence; not equivalent to Korean 60 Hz safety and EMC validation

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Critical gap — South Korea 60 Hz electrical compatibility and EMC evidence must be validated separately; China 50 Hz heat pumps are not directly compatible.

source.publisher: National Radio Research Agency / MSIT, Republic of Korea

rows.requirement: Top Runner Programme — Heat-pump HVAC SCOP Targets
rows.target_requirement: South Korea uses an energy-efficiency Top Runner programme administered through energy-policy bodies including MOTIE and KEMCO. Covered heat-pump and air-conditioning products may need to meet or document category-specific target performance such as SCOP, with Korean product classification, test conditions, reporting, and labelling controls applied separately from the ordinary KEMCO grade label.
target_standards: Applicable SCOP target criteria for heat-pump HVAC products
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly relies on GB 25454 and GB/T 7725 for COP, SCOP, and heat-pump performance evidence, CCC mandatory certification for applicable heat pumps up to 40 kW, and GB 9237 as a refrigerant safety baseline. Chinese efficiency target or label evidence is not a substitute for South Korea Top Runner classification and target documentation.
china_standards: CCC mandatory certification for applicable heat pumps up to 40 kW
rows.gap: Exporters need a South Korea-specific Top Runner applicability check before making high-efficiency or SCOP claims. The main gap is classification and calculation: China GB/T 7725 or GB 25454 data may not match Korean categories, climate assumptions, seasonal calculation boundaries, or 60 Hz test conditions.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory or target-managed for covered product classes under South Korea Top Runner and energy efficiency policy
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for applicable Chinese efficiency categories; target system is not equivalent to South Korea Top Runner

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Gap — South Korea Top Runner SCOP or target-performance treatment must be checked separately from China efficiency reports and KEMCO grade labelling.

source.publisher: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE), Republic of Korea
